What does 물광 (mul-gwang) actually mean on a Seoul clinic menu?

Most lines on a Korean clinic menu name the goal, not the method. That's why two clinics can sell different things under the same word.

물광 · “water glow” — usually small injections of a hydrating gel into the skin. Glow, not volume.
윤곽 주사 · “contour injection” — the name is the goal. What's inside varies by clinic.
리프팅 · “lifting” — usually an ultrasound or radiofrequency device, sometimes threads. Not a surgical facelift.
레이저 토닝 · “laser toning” — low-energy laser, usually planned as a course.

The question that turns a menu into a plan:
“What exactly is this, and what will it change for me?”

Seoul clinic, decoded #1. Next: the consent form.
